manuscript_title: Response geometry under community reorganization: from ecological possibility to mechanistic resolution in island plant–pollinator systems
significance_statement: Ecological perturbations are often summarized by average effects even when response direction changes among organismal states and realized communities. We show that response direction is relational rather than intrinsic: turnover reshapes the response geometry, starting state is evaluated against the community actually realized, local filtering can reallocate branches, and downstream assurance mainly modifies magnitude. Prespecified seed, time-horizon and trait-adjustment sensitivities preserve the structural ordering, while mixed geometry persists when initial pollinator richness is equalized. A source audit then shows an outcome-rich but process-poor literature, especially for partner arrival/replacement, and an Izu analysis localizes the current empirical signal to source state plus background community composition rather than beyond-composition sorting.
data_availability: Primary numerical results derive from frozen synthetic simulation outputs, a prespecified relational-robustness audit, a frozen 25-entry source-readiness audit and a source-locked secondary analysis of published Izu plant–pollinator data. The anonymous reviewer archive contains the journal-facing manuscript, corrected Supporting Information, exact interaction-kernel identity audit, frozen response-geometry and threshold results, seed/horizon/trait-adjustment/equal-richness sensitivities, deterministic figure inputs, external source-readiness records, Izu source/recovery gates, structural-audit records and analysis scripts needed to inspect the reported claim boundaries. Data and custom code supporting review are prepared for first submission in the anonymous review archive; before final publication, accepted code and frozen analysis materials will be deposited in an immutable versioned public archive with a persistent DOI.
